promptHistory:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: actual transparent 4-column by 4-row game character sprite atlas, sixteen full-body poses of ONE hero.
Input image 1: existing eight-hero atlas; use ONLY the identified hero as identity and costume reference. Input image 2: existing Admiral Yi 4x4 atlas; use it as the exact quality, camera, scale, spacing and painterly finish reference, never copy Yi's costume.
Primary request: derive a NEW consistent sixteen-pose atlas of the specified Korean hero for an elevated fixed-camera tower-defense battlefield. Beautiful premium painted animated-film character rendering, rich carefully designed broad colors, refined facial features and folds, natural material separation, compact heroic adult proportions about 4.5 heads tall. High orthographic camera tilted down approximately 40 degrees. Cool soft ambient light and warm gentle upper-left key, subtle modeling without noisy grain or plastic shine.
Layout: exactly four evenly spaced columns and four evenly spaced rows on a genuinely transparent RGBA background. Same character, same equipment, same body height and same foot baseline within EVERY cell. At least 10% clear transparent margin per cell and broad transparent gutters. Full head, feet, garment, equipment and weapon remain inside each cell. Do not let any sprite touch its neighbor. No ground shadow; the game supplies shadows.
Column 1 faces diagonally toward screen LOWER RIGHT, front three-quarter. Column 2 faces diagonally away toward screen UPPER RIGHT, right/back three-quarter; show more back and right shoulder. Column 3 faces diagonally away toward screen UPPER LEFT, back/left three-quarter with back clearly visible. Column 4 faces toward screen LOWER LEFT, left/front three-quarter. Every row MUST retain these same four facing directions.
Row 1: relaxed standing ready pose. Row 2: walking stride with left foot forward. Row 3: opposite walking stride with right foot forward, visibly different limbs and robe folds from row 2. Row 4: the hero's specified attack action aiming consistently along each column's facing direction.
Constraints: never change the character's face, age, color scheme, clothing or equipment between cells. No other hero. No lettering, numbers, labels, grid lines, floor, scenery, glow effects, projectiles, vignette, black backdrop, checkerboard or decorative frame. Deliver the production cutout atlas itself, not a mockup.
Gutter priority: reduce the character's scale so full weapon poses occupy at most 78% of each cell's height and 82% of width. Keep ALL four rows and columns separated by fully transparent empty bands; feather tips, sword tips and cloth cannot enter a gutter.
Subject and attack identity: AN JUNG-GEUN, THIRD hero on BOTTOM ROW of input image 1: young adult Korean patriot with parted short black hair, small black mustache and neat goatee, long dark navy/charcoal Western-style overcoat over a charcoal suit and waistcoat, white shirt and dark tie, polished black leather shoes. No hat and no armor. Carries ONE compact period-style brown-steel pistol in his right hand. Attack row: stand firmly and extend the right arm to aim the pistol along each column's facing direction, controlled one-handed marksmanship, left hand supporting balance near the torso. No muzzle flash, smoke or projectile baked into the sprite.
Input image 3: spacing reference ONLY. Use the very generous transparent spacing and smaller per-cell figure size of image 3, leaving broad blank margins like image 3. Do not copy image 3's green costume, feather fan or character. Keep the hero identity defined from image 1.
